why_some_numbers_have_no_macro: Whole numbers below 100, and round numbers that double as percentages or durations elsewhere in the papers, have no macro: the build would otherwise refuse the same digits wherever another section types them as an ordinary number. The papers print them as words or as plain digits; each is listed here with its source so that it can be checked.
limits: Each score is from one recording, on a part of that recording kept out of fitting; none is a test on another animal or person.
These models were scored against a linear fit on the same brain recording, not against a forecast made from the target's own history.
The muscle decoder's target is a rescaled envelope with no physical unit, although the source file labels it in millivolts. Its mean hides a weakest channel far below it.
The earlier finger classifier's own-session test had been looked at in an earlier pilot; a version built to carry to another day, with no local examples, scored at the chance rate there.

The different-day study looks backwards (the new day is two days earlier than the day the old model was fitted on), and its eight outcomes share one set of test windows that has been inspected: they are not eight independent experiments.
A band that holds 90% of readings one output at a time holds far fewer moments at which all outputs are inside at once.

Before the event streams of the reach-to-grasp recording were put in time order, the muscle-decoder, shared-model and band results built on them were wrong; those results were withdrawn and the numbers here are from the corrected pipeline.
